newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-DANES SPRING SURPRISES AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-DANES SPRING SURPRISES AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Denmark claimed four of the eight quarter-final spots in the men's singles at the world badminton championships on Thursday after Peter Gade Christensen and Peter Rasmussen scored upset wins.

Olympic champion Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen, the number two seed, also eased through, and Thomas Stuer-Lauridsen completed the quartet when he gained a walkover following the withdrawal through illness of top seed Dong Jiong of China.
Stuer-Lauridsen now meets defending champion Heryanto Arbi from Indonesia for a place in the last four.
But in the women's singles it was a Dane who made a shock early exit, with European champion Camilla Martin, the world number four, going out in three games to China's Han Jingna.

Gade Christensen, the 20-year-old rising star who defeated Hoyer-Larsen in the Taiwan Open final in January, collected another great scalp when he battled back from dropping the opening game to defeat the number seed from Taiwan, Fung Permadi.
Gade Christensen, who won the Scottish Open last November, made it a happy return to Glasgow with a 9-15 15-7 15-9 victory in exactly one hour.
Helped by a vociferous Danish support, Christensen never dropped a point from 7-9 down in the decider. His reward is a match against third seeded Sun Jun, from China, a fomer world junior champion.
Martin, playing in the neighbouring court to Christensen, failed to find similar inspiration against China's Han, going down 11-3 7-11 7-11.

Martin, 23, appeared in total control when she took the opening game in just seven minutes. But, at 1-4 down in the second, she lunged for a shot and hurt her right leg -- a setback that marked the start of her downfall.

Han drew level by taking the second game 11-7, and raced away to lead 4-0 in the third. Martin did battle back to 5-5, but then produced a string of errors to allow the Chinese to forge 9-5 in front and she comfortably went on to claim the last eight place.

Susi Susanti, the ever-popular 1993 champion, stuttered against China's Zeng Yaqoing. But after collecting just three points in the first game and trailing early in the second, the world number five went on to win 3-11 12-10 11-3.

In the men's tournament, Hoyer-Larsen, with his odds of gaining a first world title having gained a considerable boost with Dong's withdrawal, was never behind in defeating China's Luo Yigang 15-12 15-10.
Earlier, Rasmussen had claimed his place in the quarter-finals with a 15-8 8-15 15-1 win over number four seed, Indra Wijaya of Indonesia.
